nodes.description: The initiating lesion in the truncating-allele families is a heterozygous premature stop codon in TPM4. Tropomyosins act as dimers whose N- and C-terminal overlap is needed for filament formation, so a truncated product cannot copolymerize with actin, and patient platelets carry roughly half the normal amount of TPM4.2 mRNA and protein, which is a haploinsufficiency lesion. The mouse Plt53 splice allele and a targeted knockout give the same phenotype in a dose-dependent way. Whether the two missense alleles also act through reduced dosage, or by a dominant-negative effect, is not settled.

nodes.description: The terminal step of platelet biogenesis is where TPM4 deficiency acts. Megakaryocyte numbers, proliferation and maturation are preserved, and in mice megakaryocytes are actually more numerous, but proplatelet formation falls by about 20% in heterozygous and 40% in homozygous mouse megakaryocytes and in proportion to residual TPM4 in knocked-down human megakaryocytes. Mutant megakaryocytes extend few or no proplatelet branches, and the tips that do form are enlarged. Phosphorylated (inactive) cofilin is reduced in mutant cells, consistent with tropomyosin normally shielding actin filaments from cofilin severing, but which cytoskeletal step is rate-limiting has not been shown. An ex vivo lung perfusion study further suggests TPM4 is needed for the final fragmentation of large anuclear megakaryocyte fragments into platelets.

nodes.description: Circulating TPM4-deficient platelets remodel their actin cytoskeleton poorly on activation. Human p.Gln108* platelets spread less after TRAP-6 or collagen-related peptide stimulation and the residual TPM4 fails to move into filopodia and lamellipodia; mouse Tpm4 mutant platelets spread fully on fibrinogen but more slowly, and show partial degradation of filamin A and calpain-type cleavage of actinin 1, with frequent vacuoles suggesting fragility. Aggregation, integrin inside-out activation and granule secretion in response to agonists are preserved in truncating-allele carriers and in mice. The authors note the delayed spreading may partly reflect the larger platelet size.
